problem: Given a static set of N integer keys known in advance, build a lookup table that answers membership/index queries in guaranteed O(1) worst-case time with no per-query collisions and near-N space.
obvious_approach: Use a hash table with a good general-purpose hash function, accepting expected O(1) but worst-case O(N) on collisions, over-provisioning the array to keep load factor low.
reframe_type: offline-construction (hashing as search over functions; perfect hashing)

problem: Find all occurrences of a pattern P in a text T and also handle approximate matching where up to k characters may differ, computing all alignment scores efficiently.
obvious_approach: Rabin-Karp rolling hash for exact matching, or an O(nk) kangaroo/Landau-Vishkin method with suffix-tree LCP queries for k-mismatches.
reframe_type: cross-domain import (string matching as convolution via FFT)

problem: Given a directed graph with possibly negative edge weights but no negative cycles, answer many shortest-path queries between arbitrary node pairs.
obvious_approach: Bellman-Ford per source (O(VE) each) or Floyd-Warshall (O(V^3)), accepting that fast Dijkstra cannot handle negative weights.
reframe_type: duality / gauge transform (node potentials reweight to non-negative; Johnson's)

problem: Support a sequence of N elements with split-at-position, concatenate, and indexed access all in O(log N), to cheaply cut and join large editable text buffers.
obvious_approach: Dynamic array / gap buffer (O(1) index but O(N) split/concat by copying), or a doubly linked list (O(1) splice but O(N) index and poor cache behavior).
reframe_type: representation shift (index -> rank in a size-augmented balanced tree; rope)

problem: Numerically integrate the trajectory of a frictionless orbiting body over millions of timesteps so the orbit does not slowly spiral in or out due to accumulated error.
obvious_approach: Use a high-order Runge-Kutta integrator (RK4) with a small timestep for low local truncation error.

problem: Solve Ax=b for a large sparse symmetric positive-definite A that you can only access through a black-box function returning the matrix-vector product Av; you never see the entries of A.
obvious_approach: Reconstruct A column-by-column by probing with basis vectors e_i (N matvecs), then factor it with Cholesky/LU.
reframe_type: recast algebra as optimization (minimize the quadratic; Conjugate Gradient on matvecs)
